name: Kinema
subtitle: fermented soybeans cooked with tomato and chilli, pungent and deeply savoury

ingredients.note: standing in for kinema, fermented whole soybeans; the flavour is milder but the base is right

prepNotes: Kinema is a Limbu and Nepali ferment of the eastern Himalaya, close kin to Japanese natto. It smells strong and tastes savoury rather than sour.
Real kinema cannot be improvised. This uses crumbled tofu for texture and leans on the mustard oil and chilli for character; it is a version, not the thing itself.

steps.text: Fry the crumbled tofu in the mustard oil until browned and dry at the edges, 8 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic, ginger and green chillies and cook until soft.
Add the turmeric and tomato and cook down until the oil separates, about 8 minutes.
Add 150ml water and simmer 5 minutes into a thick, spoonable curry.
Season and finish with coriander. Serve with rice.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat to a full simmer.
